# DataFn Documentation

> Self-hosted data sync SDK with offline-first storage, reactive signals, capability-driven schemas, and a structured query language (DFQL). Works with TypeScript, Python, and Swift.

This document is intended for large language models and agentic developer tools. It contains an outline of the DataFn documentation with deep-links to each page; for the full content see `llms-full.txt`.

## Ai Resources

- [Claude](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/claude): Wire DataFn into Claude Code and Claude Desktop with project memory, raw-markdown lookups, and MCP.
- [Codex / GPT-based assistants](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/codex): Wire DataFn into OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Continue.dev.
- [Cursor](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/cursor): Wire DataFn into Cursor with project rules, raw-markdown lookups, and MCP.
- [llms.txt / llms-full.txt](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/llms-txt): Machine-readable artifacts that turn the DataFn documentation into a prompt-friendly corpus.
- [MCP Server (Experimental)](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/mcp): Expose the DataFn documentation and schema as Model Context Protocol tools for agentic clients.
- [Skills](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources/skills): Drop-in instruction files that teach AI coding assistants how to use DataFn correctly.

## Top Level

- [AI Resources](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/ai-resources): LLM-ready artifacts and agent affordances for working with DataFn through Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and other assistants.
- [CLI Overview](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli): Command-line tools for DataFn schema management and code generation.
- [Comparison](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/comparison): Where DataFn sits relative to Replicache, ElectricSQL, PowerSync, RxDB, WatermelonDB, InstantDB, Convex, TinyBase, and a Drizzle+TanStack Query stack.
- [DFQL Overview](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql): DataFn Query Language - a JSON-based query and mutation language.
- [Overview](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation): What DataFn is, what it ships, and how the pieces fit together.
- [Examples](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/examples): Working reference apps that ship with DataFn — clone, run, copy what you need.
- [Getting Started](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/getting-started): Get up and running with DataFn in minutes.
- [DataFn](https://datafn.21n.co/docs): Self-hosted data sync SDK with offline-first storage, reactive signals, and a declarative query language.
- [Quickstart](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/quickstart): Pick your stack and ship a working DataFn integration in 10 minutes.
- [Recipes](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes): Production-tested patterns for shipping with DataFn. Each recipe is self-contained: the schema, the server config, and the client glue.
- [API Reference](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference): Complete API reference for all DataFn packages.

- [CI Integration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/ci-integration): GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and CircleCI recipes for DataFn schema validation and migration.
- [Drizzle Schema Generation](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/drizzle-codegen): Generate Drizzle ORM table definitions from your schema.
- [Environment Profiles](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/env-profiles): Manage dev, staging, and production configuration with the CLI.
- [Generate](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/generate): Generate TypeScript types and database schemas from your DataFn schema.
- [Multi-Environment Workflows](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/multi-env): Promote schemas and migrations across dev → staging → production safely.
- [datafn schema-diff](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/schema-diff): Compare two schema versions and produce a structured diff.
- [datafn schema-migrate](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/schema-migrate): Generate and apply schema migration plans.
- [Type Generation](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/type-codegen): Generate TypeScript interfaces from your schema.
- [Validate](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/cli/validate): Validate your DataFn schema file.

## Dfql

- [Aggregations](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/aggregations): Compute aggregate values over record sets.
- [Filters](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/filters): Filter records with comparison, set, string, and logical operators.
- [Mutations](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/mutations): DFQL write operations, including capability-aware lifecycle and sharing mutations.
- [Pagination](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/pagination): Paginate query results with limit/offset or cursors.
- [Queries](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/queries): Retrieve data with DFQL queries.
- [Fields](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/schema/fields): Configure field types, validation constraints, and behavior.
- [Schema Definition](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/schema): Define and validate your DataFn schema, including capability-driven behavior.
- [Relations](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/schema/relations): Define, query, and mutate relationships between resources.
- [Resources](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/schema/resources): Define resources, permissions, and per-resource capabilities.
- [System Fields](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/schema/system-fields): Capability-injected lifecycle fields and server ownership rules.
- [Search](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/search): Provider-backed full-text search for DFQL and client cross-resource search.
- [Select and Expand](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/select): Control which fields are returned and expand relations.
- [Sorting](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/sorting): Sort query results by one or more fields.
- [Transactions](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/dfql/transactions): Execute atomic sequences of queries and mutations.

## Documentation

- [Change Tracking](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/change-tracking): Track mutations for incremental sync.
- [Debouncing](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/debouncing): Coalesce rapid mutations for better performance.
- [Error Handling](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/error-handling): Structured error handling across client and server.
- [Guards](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/guards): Optimistic concurrency control with conditional mutations.
- [Idempotency](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/idempotency): Prevent duplicate mutations with idempotency tracking.
- [Security](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/advanced/security): Security measures built into DataFn.
- [Background Sync](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/background): Background app refresh, silent push, and sync-on-resume for the Apple runtime.
- [CloudKit Sync](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/cloudkit): Replace the DataFn server with iCloud — same client API, Apple-managed sync.
- [CoreData Store](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/coredata): Where DataFn keeps records on Apple devices, and how the schema maps to CoreData entities.
- [Apple Runtime](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple): DataFn on iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS — CoreData persistence, SwiftUI observation, and optional CloudKit sync.
- [App Intents](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/intents): Expose DataFn records to Siri, Shortcuts, Focus filters, and Spotlight via App Intents.
- [Observation](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/observation): DatafnRuntimeObservationSource and DatafnObservedQuery — how SwiftUI sees DataFn records.
- [Apple Runtime Setup](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/setup): Bootstrap DatafnAppleRuntime in an iOS or macOS app.
- [SwiftUI Integration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/swiftui): Drop DataFn observed queries into SwiftUI views, bind to forms, and handle navigation.
- [WebView Bridge](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/apple/webview-bridge): DatafnWKWebViewBridgeHost — let a WebView dispatch mutations into native CoreData.
- [Capabilities](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/capabilities): Opt-in resource behaviors for lifecycle fields, mutation operations, auto-filters, and sharing.
- [Events](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/events): Subscribe to mutation and sync events.
- [Framework Adapters](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/frameworks): Connect DataFn to your UI framework with thin adapter packages.
- [Key-Value Store](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/kv): A built-in key-value API with signals and debounce support.
- [Mutations](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/mutations): Execute core and capability-aware mutations from the DataFn client.
- [Queries](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/queries): Query data from the server or local storage.
- [Client Setup](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/setup): Create and configure a DataFn client instance.
- [Signals](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/signals): Reactive query results that auto-refresh on mutations.
- [Tables](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/tables): Per-resource handles with capability-gated methods.
- [Transactions](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/client/transactions): Execute atomic sequences of queries and mutations.
- [Database Adapters](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/database/adapters): Connect DataFn to your database.
- [Drizzle Adapter](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/database/drizzle): Use Drizzle ORM as your database backend.
- [Database Transactions](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/database/transactions): Atomic operations with database transactions.
- [Deploy to Cloudflare Workers](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/cloudflare-workers): Run DataFn at the edge with D1, Hyperdrive, or your own Postgres.
- [Docker](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/docker): Run DataFn in a container. Foundation for self-hosted, on-prem, or bring-your-own platform.
- [Deploy to Fly.io](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/fly): Run DataFn on Fly with managed Postgres and multi-region scaling.
- [Production & Deploy](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy): Where DataFn fits in your hosting stack and how to deploy it on the major platforms.
- [Kubernetes](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/kubernetes): Production-shaped DataFn on Kubernetes with Helm, HPA, and graceful rollouts.
- [Deploy to Railway](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/railway): Zero-config DataFn deploys on Railway with managed Postgres and Redis.
- [Scaling](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/scaling): Sequence store, WebSocket broadcasting, multi-region, and the bottleneck pattern.
- [Deploy to Vercel](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/deploy/vercel): Run DataFn on Vercel with Next.js or SvelteKit and a managed Postgres.
- [SPV2 Migration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/migrations/spv2): Roll out Sharing Permissions V2 safely with backfill, dual-read, dual-write, and rollback controls.
- [Namespaces](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/namespaces): Isolate data between tenants, users, or any grouping with composable namespace strings.
- [Client Search Plugin](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/plugins/client-search): Built-in plugin for client-side full-text search with provider-backed or legacy MiniSearch mode.
- [Custom Plugins](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/plugins/custom-plugins): Build your own DataFn plugins.
- [Plugin System](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/plugins/overview): Extend DataFn with pluggable hooks.
- [Field-Level Authorization](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/field-level-authz): Declarative per-field access control via the permissions policy on each resource.
- [Security](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security): DataFn's security model: layered defenses from rate limiting through field-level authorization.
- [Input Sanitization](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/input-sanitization): Prototype pollution, path traversal, and type confusion — what DataFn rejects.
- [Layered Security Model](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/layered-model): How DataFn's seven defense layers chain together — and why each layer exists.
- [Namespace Isolation](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/namespace-isolation): Row-level multi-tenancy that's automatic, transparent, and impossible to bypass through DFQL.
- [Payload Limits](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/payload-limits): Body size, complexity caps, and per-request resource limits.
- [Production Checklist](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/production-checklist): The minimum security configuration for a production DataFn deployment.
- [Rate Limiting](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/rate-limiting): Per-endpoint rate limits backed by Redis or memory.
- [Request Authorization](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/request-authz): The authorize callback — coarse-grained gating per request.
- [WebSocket Security](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/security/websocket-security): How DataFn protects WebSocket connections: auth at upgrade, namespace lock, connection caps, and heartbeats.
- [Authorization](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/authorization): Control access to resources and fields.
- [Observability](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/observability): Monitor server performance with timing events.
- [Rate Limiting](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/rate-limiting): Protect your server with configurable rate limits.
- [REST API](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/rest-api): Optional RESTful endpoint wrappers.
- [Routes](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/routes): HTTP endpoints provided by the DataFn server.
- [Server Setup](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/setup): Create and configure a DataFn server.
- [Validation](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/validation): Request validation and schema compliance checks.
- [WebSockets](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/server/websockets): Real-time updates via WebSocket connections.
- [Sharing](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sharing): Guide to Sharing Permissions: namespace, principal, visibility, scope grants, relation inheritance, and compatibility behavior.
- [Custom Storage](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/storage/custom): Implement your own storage adapter.
- [IndexedDB](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/storage/indexeddb): Persistent browser storage via IndexedDB.
- [Memory Storage](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/storage/memory): In-memory storage for testing and SSR.
- [Storage Overview](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/storage/overview): Persistent offline storage adapters.
- [Clone Up](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/clone-up): Upload offline changes to the remote server.
- [Clone](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/clone): Full dataset retrieval for initial client setup.
- [Conflict Resolution](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/conflict-resolution): How DataFn resolves competing writes: last-writer-wins, version guards, and explicit merge policies.
- [Cross-Tab Sync](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/cross-tab): Synchronize state between browser tabs.
- [Hydration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/hydration): Configure startup data loading strategy.
- [Offline-First](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/offline-first): Build applications that work without a network connection.
- [Ordering Guarantees](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/ordering-guarantees): What DataFn promises about the order of operations across clients.
- [Sync Overview](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/overview): Understand the DataFn synchronization architecture.
- [Pull and Push](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/pull-push): Incremental synchronization between client and server.
- [Retry and Backoff](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/retry-and-backoff): How the DataFn client retries failed sync operations, and how to tune it.
- [Schema Migration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/schema-migration): Evolving the schema while clients are connected — adding, renaming, deprecating fields.
- [Sequence Store](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/sequence-store): Where serverSeq lives, why it matters, and how to pick the right backend.
- [Sharing Sync Lifecycle](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/sync/sharing-sync-lifecycle): How offline clients observe grant, revoke, backfill, push, and pull behavior in Sharing Permissions V2.
- [Troubleshooting](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/troubleshooting): The 15 failure modes you'll hit in production — and how to fix them.
- [Sharing Patterns](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/documentation/use-cases/sharing-patterns): Canonical namespace, visibility, grant, and sync patterns for Collections, Memotron, Selftron, Pointron, Finatron, Feedtron, and Compoundum.

## Recipes

- [Recipe: Audit Logging](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/audit-logging): Capability-driven audit fields plus outbound logging to your audit pipeline.
- [Recipe: AuthFn Integration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/authfn-integration): Wire AuthFn sessions into DataFn's authorize and namespaceProvider.
- [Recipe: Chat App](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/chat-app): Append-only messages, cursor pagination, WebSocket live updates.
- [Recipe: Document Collaboration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/document-collab): Per-document presence, conflict-free edits, and a roadmap to true CRDT collaboration.
- [Recipe: Encryption at Rest](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/encryption-at-rest): Field-level encryption via plugins, with the server holding only ciphertext.
- [Recipe: FileFn Integration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/filefn-integration): Attach files to DataFn records — uploads, lifecycle, deletion.
- [Recipe: Kanban Board](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/kanban-board): Ordered lists with drag-and-drop, position fields, and atomic moves via transact.
- [Recipe: Multi-tenant SaaS](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/multi-tenant-saas): Namespace per tenant; deriving namespaces from auth; cross-tenant query isolation.
- [Recipe: Offline Conflict Resolution](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/offline-conflicts): Last-writer-wins, version guards, and explicit merge policies for offline-first writes.
- [Recipe: Optimistic UI](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/optimistic-ui): Snappy mutations with deterministic rollback when the server rejects.
- [Recipe: Presence and Live Cursors](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/presence-cursors): Ephemeral state alongside DataFn's persisted state.
- [Recipe: SearchFn Integration](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/searchfn-integration): Cross-resource search via the SearchProvider interface, backed by SearchFn.
- [Recipe: Sharing Flows](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/sharing-flows): Invite-by-email, link-share, share-with-role — all on top of the shareable capability.
- [Recipe: Testing Patterns](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/testing): Deterministic sync, fixture seeding, and mock clients for unit and integration tests.
- [Recipe: Todo App](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/todo-app): The minimum viable end-to-end DataFn app: schema, server, client, optimistic UI.
- [Recipe: List Virtualization](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/recipes/virtualization): Subscriptions over windowed slices for large lists.

- [Errors Reference](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/errors): Canonical error code matrix: what each code means, what causes it, and how to fix it.

- [HTTP Routes Reference](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/routes): Canonical reference for every route exposed by the DataFn server: method, path, request shape, response shape, and error codes.

- [Execution Engine](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/execution): Query and mutation execution internals.

- [WebSocket Manager](https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/websocket): WebSocket manager reference.
